_doc: This repository's factory settings. render.py renders .github/workflows/factory-*.yml from templates/ with them (and planning.json's database); the factory's scripts and workflow_policy.py read them at run time. The app, image and smoke.echo_host values are placeholders: Enablement fills them with your organization's factory App, job image and echo service, and bootstrap.py applies nothing until it has. The runner labels and environment names are defaults every project in the organization shares (runners.ci is the CI tier's, for a project's own self-hosted CI jobs; host/setup.sh's TIER=ci); set the stack block for this project (process/factory.md, Enablement). Edit this or a template, then run render.py; CI's render check refuses a workflow edited by hand.

release._doc: How production gets this project's code (process/factory.md, D4 rule 13). The default, a release branch: every host that serves production deploys it, and CD's merge of a PR into it is the deploy. A release gate deploys partway through a plan, and a plan's Release section gets a release PR into it when CD merges the plan's execution PR (factory-release-pr.yml). Create it at main's tip, with its two rulesets, before the first plan that releases (Enablement steps 2 and 9). Empty is the fallback, for a production host that can't follow a branch yet: the broker deploys an execution PR's head in a gate, before CD merges it.

smoke._doc: factory-smoke's stand-in service: a host that echoes each request's headers back as indented JSON (httpbin's /headers), so the credential-mask and services probes can see what the sandbox proxy injected. echo/ holds its source: a Cloudflare Worker, or a small server for any container host behind HTTPS. host_probes: the runner host's own addresses (LAN, VPN, compose network gateways), space-separated, which smoke's isolation probe must find unreachable from a job; the default Docker bridge and rootless gateways are always probed.

stack._doc: The stack profile (profiles/<profile>/: the job image, install.sh, test-services.sh, with-test-services, verify) and where this project keeps what it works on. agent_job.sh reads these at run time.

fixtures._doc: Test fixtures whose source needs a secret (process/factory.md, D2 rule 7). When path is set, the implement and revise workflows run a fixtures job on a GitHub-hosted runner: it checks out the default branch, restores path from the Actions cache (key: cache_key-<hash of key_files>), and on a miss installs the apt packages and runs run with the repository secret named by secret in its environment, under that name. It refuses fixtures that hold the secret, then hands path to the agent job as an artifact, which puts it in the workspace before the agent starts. The agent job never holds the secret. path must be gitignored. Leave path empty for none.

policy._doc: Read by workflow_policy.py, which CI runs over every workflow, the project's own included (process/factory.md, Enablement step 10); no template uses these. hosted_labels: the organization's own GitHub-hosted (larger) runner labels, addressed by label, not by runner group; a listed label counts as hosted wherever the policy asks (the container rule, the App key's job, the fixtures job), so never list one a self-hosted runner can carry (self-hosted, linux, x64 and the like are refused) or a factory runner label. self_hosted_exemptions: the project's own CI jobs that may run on a self-hosted runner without the factory container, each {"workflow": "ci.yml", "job": "<job id>", "reason": "<how that runner is isolated, and why the job can't run hosted>"}; never a factory workflow, a job on the factory's runners or an agent job; the factory's secret rules still hold in it; an entry for a job that no longer exists or now runs hosted is a violation. Both empty by default.

ci._doc: The CI tier's job image (process/factory.md, Enablement step 10, The CI tier): host/setup.sh (TIER=ci) builds the project's toolchain from dockerfile with context (paths inside the repository, links included, build_args static), then ci-runner.Dockerfile puts the runner on top. One container of it runs each job, so its toolchain is what every job on the tier gets: the base must be Debian or Ubuntu, pinned by digest, and a toolchain change takes a setup run on the host. Leave dockerfile empty for no CI tier.

review._doc: Where to look (process/factory.md, Where to look): rules naming the files CD always looks at in a factory PR. A start for every stack profile; the line rules know Django's and ASP.NET Core's names, so a project on another framework adds its own. Add the project's always-high areas as rules with paths, such as the code that computes money.
